questions.questionText: In an economy, the number of people in work is unchanged but the rate of growth of labour productivity slows from 2.3% to 0.4%. It can be concluded that there will be an increase in
Using the data in Extract D (Figure 3), calculate the difference between the percentage increase in GDP for Japan and the USA between 2001 and 2023. Give your answer to one decimal place.
Which one of the following statements concerning short-run economic growth and long-run economic growth is correct?
options: Short-run growth is inflationary whereas long-run growth will cause a fall in the average price level
Short-run growth may occur independently of the government whereas long-run growth is only achieved as a result of government policy
Short-run growth may occur when governments use demand-side policies but these do not affect long-run growth
Short-run growth may reduce spare capacity whereas long-run growth increases productive capacity

options: a fall in the exchange rate.
a fall in the trade surplus.
a rise in the foreign currency price of exports.
a rise in the volume of imports.

questions.questionText: Figure 2 shows the long-run trend rate of unemployment and the actual rate of unemployment in a country over a period of time. At which one of the following points was the economy most likely to be in the recession phase of its economic cycle?
Figure 1 shows the rate of unemployment in an economy over a period of time. At which one of the following points was the economy most likely to be in the recovery phase of the economic cycle?
Explain possible reasons why a country may enter a recession.

Country W is operating at its normal capacity level of output. When one of its trading partners experiences economic growth, this leads to a rise in demand for Country W’s exports. All other things being equal, what is the most likely consequence of this for Country W?
options: A fall in employment and a reduction in cost-push inflation
A negative output gap and a period of disinflation
A positive output gap and an increase in demand-pull inflation
An increase in unemployment and a fall in the price level

questions.questionText: Figure 2 shows the aggregate demand (AD), short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) and long-run aggregate supply (LRAS) curves for an economy. All other things being equal, which one of the following is the most likely consequence for firms if an increase in government spending shifts the aggregate demand curve from AD to AD2?

A government introduces a number of supply-side policies that increase the size of the country's working population and labour productivity. All other things being equal, which one of the following statements identifies the most likely effects of the policies on the country's economy?
options: An increase in real national income and a reduction in the balance of payments deficit
An increase in short-run economic growth and inflation
An increase in the trend rate of economic growth and a growing balance of payments deficit
A reduction in unemployment and an increase in inflation

questions.questionText: An economy's long-run trend rate of economic growth in real gross domestic product (GDP) is 2.8% per annum. In 2018, the economy's actual real GDP was equal to its trend level of real GDP. Table 4 shows the economy's actual rate of growth in real GDP over a five-year period. All other things being equal, in which year was the economy likely to experience the most inflationary pressure?
Explain how the data in Extract A (Figure 2), show that Ireland’s economy performed better than the economies of France and Spain in 2021.
Which one of the following is most likely to be used to identify a phase of the economic cycle?

Table 3 shows the planned change in government spending, the size of the output gap and the size of the multiplier in four economies, W, X, Y and Z. All other things being equal, in which one of the economies, W, X, Y or Z, will the planned change in government spending eliminate the economy’s output gap?
Table 4 shows the percentage change in real GDP in an economy in the four years 2016 to 2019. Over the period 2016 to 2019, which one of the following can be concluded from Table 4?
Explain possible causes of economic growth.
Evaluate the view that economic growth usually leads to an improvement in living standards.

An economy experiences a low trend rate of economic growth, no output gap and a fall in total hours worked. In these circumstances, which one of the following combinations of events is most likely to occur?

An economy operating at its long-run productive capacity at the start of 2020 has a trend rate of growth of 6% per year. Real GDP increases by 2% in 2021 and 10% in 2022. Which one of the following accurately describes the position of the economy at the end of each year?
An economy experiences an increasing negative output gap. Which one of the following combinations of outcomes most accurately describes the likely effects of this?
Explain the main problems for an economy of having a large positive output gap.

Assess policies which can be used to reduce cyclical instability in the UK.
Which one of the following combinations of possible shocks: A, B, C, or D, is most likely to move an economy from a negative output gap to a positive output gap? An unexpected increase in
options: productivity growth combined with a larger than expected decrease in inflation.
the exchange rate combined with an unexpected fall in business confidence.
the government’s budget surplus combined with a downturn in world trade.
the marginal propensity to consume combined with a fall in the exchange rate.

questions.questionText: In 2019, an economy operating at full capacity on its long-run aggregate supply curve grew at its trend growth rate of 5% per annum. It had a national income of £200 billion. In 2020, the economy experienced 2% actual growth. It follows that in 2020 there was
options: a negative output gap equal to £4 billion.
a negative output gap equal to £6 billion.
a positive output gap equal to £4 billion.
a positive output gap equal to £6 billion.

questions.questionText: Explain how an appreciation of its currency is likely to affect a country’s rate of economic growth.
Figure 1 shows three aggregate demand (AD) curves, a short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) curve and a long-run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve. In Figure 1, when
options: aggregate demand shifts from AD1 to AD2, cyclical unemployment is likely to be eliminated.
aggregate demand shifts from AD1 to AD3, the rate of economic growth is equal to (Y3 – Y1).
the economy is producing at Y1, there is a positive output gap.
the economy is producing at Y2, there is no unemployment.

questions.questionText: Explain how a sustained slowdown in the world economy is likely to affect living standards in the UK.

An economy has recently recovered from a recession and closed its negative output gap. The government would now like to increase the trend rate of economic growth. Which one of the following policies is likely to be the most effective?
In which one of the following situations is there most likely to be cyclical unemployment in an economy?
Figure 4 shows the performance of an economy through time. As the economy moves from point A to point B, it can be concluded that
options: the economy has completed one economic cycle.
the level of GDP per head has risen.
the rate of economic growth has increased.
the trend rate of growth is higher.

The diagram below shows the aggregate demand curve (AD), short-run aggregate supply curve (SRAS), and long-run aggregate supply curve (LRAS) for an economy. The current level of real GDP is Y. Which one of the following policies is most likely, in the short run, to bring the economy closer to its normal capacity level of output?
options: An increase in the target rate of inflation
Higher government spending on vocational education
Lower rates of tax on manufacturing businesses
New schemes to encourage more household saving

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the actual level of real GDP and the trend level of real GDP over time for an economy. The economy starts its recovery from recession at point M. After several years of growth the economy reaches point N. All other things being equal, which one of the following is the most likely consequence of the economy’s growth path between points M and N?
options: A decrease in the level of interest rates due to deflation.
A decrease in the rate of inflation due to increased output.
An increase in investment due to the accelerator process.
An increase in the value of the multiplier due to a rise in the savings ratio.

questions.questionText: The table below shows different combinations of changes in the rate of interest and the government’s budget position. The economy has a negative output gap. All other things being equal, which one of the combinations of policies, A, B, C or D, is most likely to reduce the economy’s negative output gap?
The diagram below shows an economic cycle and the trend level of real GDP. Which point represents the economy producing at its normal capacity level of output?
Inflationary pressures are normally low when an economy has a negative output gap. The most likely explanation for this is that
options: consumers’ spending on imports and the exchange rate rise.
the Bank of England may cut bank rate and increase the money supply.
the government’s tax revenue falls and spending on benefits increases.
unemployment is high and firms have excess capacity.

questions.questionText: The table below shows the index of real GDP for the UK before and after the 2008–09 financial crisis. From the data it can be inferred that in the UK
options: real GDP fell by 2.5% between 2007 and 2011.
the annual rate of inflation was minus 1.1% in 2008.
the rate of economic growth was lower in 2011 than in 2010.
total output of the economy fell by 5.2% between 2007 and 2009.

Which one of the following would be most likely to generate growth in an economy without producing an increase in inflation?
options: A decrease in the exchange rate
An increase in the budget surplus
An increase in the rate of interest

In which one of the following situations could the UK be said to be experiencing a negative output gap?
options: Output per worker is lower in the UK than in the USA
Real GDP in the UK is less than the economy’s productive potential
UK firms do not have sufficient productive capacity to satisfy customer demand

questions.questionText: Which one of the following combinations, A, B, C or D, is most likely to occur in the recovery phase of the economic cycle?

The table below shows the annual percentage change in real GDP for an economy between 2013 and 2016. The long-run trend rate of growth for this economy is estimated to be 2.8%. Which one of the following statements is most likely to be correct?
options: In 2013, the economy’s negative output gap increased.
In 2014, the amount of spare capacity in the economy increased.
In 2015, the amount of spare capacity in the economy decreased.
